scenes.line1: How do you make errors easy to fix?
scenes.say: Ever wonder what makes an API error actually helpful? Let's break down how to design error responses that clients love.

scenes.label: Clarity
scenes.sub: Structured errors help clients debug fast.
scenes.say: Clear, structured errors make it way easier for clients to debug and handle problems gracefully.
The standard way is RFC 7807. It uses fields like type, title, status, and detail to give clients all the context they need.

scenes.title: Out of credit
scenes.say: Here's a real example. The client sees exactly what went wrong and why, so they can respond or show a clear message.

scenes.question: What's wrong with just sending status codes?
scenes.wrong: Clients can always figure it out.
scenes.right: Without details, clients can't debug or show users helpful info.
scenes.say: Don't fall for this: just sending a status code isn't enough. Clients need details to actually handle errors well.
